Voter Service & Polling Centers

See below for a list of Voter Service and Polling Centers (VSPCs) in Arapahoe County and their hours of operation for the November 3, 2026 General Election.

We encourage voters to vote their mail ballot and drop it off in a video-monitored, secure 24-hr drop box to avoid lines or any other issues that may prevent you returning your ballot by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

Residents of Arapahoe County may use any of our VSPCs for the November 3, 2026 General Election. There are no assigned polling places. You must bring an acceptable form of ID.

Voter Service and Polling Centers are open from October 19th to November 3rd depending on their phase.

- Phase 1 VSPCs are open from October 19th to November 3rd at 7:00 pm.
- Phase 2 VSPCs are open from October 30th to November 3rd at 7:00 pm.
- Phase 3 VSPCs are open from November 2nd to November 3rd at 7:00 pm.
See the list below to view the hours of operation for each VSPC.

NOTE: VSPCs are closed on Saturday, October 24th; Sunday, October 25th; and Sunday, November 1st, but you can drop off your ballot at a Ballot Drop location.

Enter your address to find your nearest VSPC location.

*Curbside Ballot Pickup service offered at some locations. 

Services available at all VSPCs:

  • Drop-off a voted mail-in ballot
  • Register to vote in-person
  • Update your voter registration
  • Request a replacement ballot if your ballot was damaged or missing
  • Request to vote in-person
  • Language interpretation services
  • Vote on an accessible electronic ballot marking device. See details below regarding our accessible services for voters with a disability
  • Vote with assistance from a caregiver or Election Judge

Check wait times here

Accessibility: Voters with a disability

Every VSPC is HAVA/ADA accessible and offers several accessible voting interfaces that allow voters with various disabilities to effectively vote, review their choices, and cast a paper ballot in a private and independent manner. Voters may request any of the following: 

  • Wheelchair-accessible voting booth
  • Audio ballot and headphones
  • Large font size and/or high contrast on ballot marking devices
  • Ability to connect to a voter's sip and puff device or paddles

Election Judges are also available to assist voters upon request.
